name: Thyme
description: Thymus vulgaris. A low, broad but compact rounded cushion with tiny paired opposite oval gray-green leaves on fine woody, much-branched stems. The young plant has distinct short twig branches. Mature foliage is a dense fine-leaved mound, never broad basil leaves. Final stage has small pale lilac-pink blossoms scattered lightly over the mound. Use a few central basal stems gathered at one central bottom soil attachment.

name: Chives
description: Allium schoenoprasum. Many smooth slender hollow tubular leaves, narrow round tubes, bright green, tapering, gently arching in a fountain clump. NOT broad flat grass blades. No branching leaf stems. Growing stage lush green clump. Final stage has 3-5 separate taller naked flower scapes each topped by a lilac-purple spherical pompom umbel of many tiny six-tepal star flowers. Leaves all converge to a short centered basal crown.

name: Dill
description: Anethum graveolens. Upright delicate blue-green herb with extremely fine threadlike 3-4-times dissected leaves (filiform lobes), an airy ferny haze, slender ribbed central stem and delicate branches. NO broad leaves at all, NO flat lobed cilantro foliage. Growing stage upright ferny green. Final mature stage taller with flat open compound umbels of tiny yellow flowers, each radiating ribs from one point like a small umbrella, a main large umbel and 2 smaller side umbels. Single central basal stem.

name: Cilantro
description: Coriandrum sativum. Young plant has rounded fan-shaped lobed bright green basal leaves with scalloped toothed edges on slender petioles. Growing stage full leafy culinary clump, distinct flat lobed leaves. Final bolting stage keeps some broad basal lobed leaves but makes finer feathery upper foliage and branching stems carrying delicate flat compound umbels of tiny WHITE to blush flowers. Not parsley curls, not daisies. Centered basal crown with petioles arising close together.

name: Thai basil
description: Ocimum basilicum var. thyrsiflora. Slender upright branching PURPLE stems with opposite pairs of glossy narrow lanceolate pointed green leaves, slightly serrated margins and subtle purple veins. Smaller narrower leaves than sweet basil. Final mature stage has several upright purple flower spikes with small lavender-pink tubular blossoms emerging among stacked dark purple bracts. Leaves remain predominantly green, purple stems and inflorescences. Centered single branching basal stalk.
